    - text: CLASS 12 · FORMAL CALCULUS
    - heading "Increasing and Decreasing Functions" [level=1]
    - paragraph: Use derivatives to determine where a function increases, decreases, and has turning points.
    - text: 30 min ADVANCED CONCEPT graph derivative
    - article:
      - heading "FUNCTION & GRAPH" [level=3]
      - heading "f(x)=x³−3x" [level=2]
      - text: Tangent at
      - status "Tangent at -0.5": x=-0.5
      - slider "Tangent point x": "-0.5"
      - img "Increasing and decreasing cubic graph":
        - slider "Graph tangent point"
        - text: (−1, 2) (1, −2)
      - button "Zoom in graph":
        - img
      - button "Zoom out graph":
        - img
      - button "Fit graph":
        - img
      - text: Move the tangent slider or drag the black point. The right panel updates automatically.
    - complementary:
      - heading "DERIVATIVE & SIGN ANALYSIS" [level=3]
      - heading "f'(x)=3x²−3=3(x−1)(x+1)" [level=2]
      - 'heading "Step 1: Critical points" [level=4]'
      - paragraph: Solve f'(x)=0 ⇒ x=−1, x=1
      - 'heading "Step 2: Sign chart for f''(x)" [level=4]'
      - table:
        - rowgroup:
          - row "Interval (−∞,−1) (−1,1) (1,∞)":
            - columnheader "Interval"
            - columnheader "(−∞,−1)"
            - columnheader "(−1,1)"
            - columnheader "(1,∞)"
        - rowgroup:
          - row "Test point −2 0 2":
            - cell "Test point"
            - cell "−2"
            - cell "0"
            - cell "2"
          - row "f'(x) + − +":
            - cell "f'(x)"
            - cell "+"
            - cell "−"
            - cell "+"
          - row "f(x) ↗ ↘ ↗":
            - cell "f(x)"
            - cell "↗"
            - cell "↘"
            - cell "↗"
      - heading "Interval Testing" [level=4]
      - button "-2"
      - button "-0.5"
      - button "0"
      - button "0.5"
      - button "2"
      - paragraph: At x=-0.5, f'(-0.5)=-2.25
      - text: f'(x) < 0 → Decreasing The sign of f'(x) determines whether f increases or decreases.
    - article:
      - heading "CLASSIFICATION OF CRITICAL POINTS" [level=3]
      - paragraph: Use f''(x)=6x or the sign change of f'(x).
      - table:
        - rowgroup:
          - row "Point x f(x) f''(x) Sign change Conclusion":
            - columnheader "Point"
            - columnheader "x"
            - columnheader "f(x)"
            - columnheader "f''(x)"
            - columnheader "Sign change"
            - columnheader "Conclusion"
        - rowgroup:
          - row "A −1 2 −6 + → − Local maximum":
            - cell "A"
            - cell "−1"
            - cell "2"
            - cell "−6"
            - cell "+ → −"
            - cell "Local maximum"
          - row "B 1 −2 6 − → + Local minimum":
            - cell "B"
            - cell "1"
            - cell "−2"
            - cell "6"
            - cell "− → +"
            - cell "Local minimum"
      - list:
        - listitem: Increasing on (−∞,−1) and (1,∞)
        - listitem: Decreasing on (−1,1)
        - listitem: Local maximum at (−1,2)
        - listitem: Local minimum at (1,−2)
      - text: These intervals and turning points are confirmed by both derivative and graph.
    - article:
      - heading "COMMON MISCONCEPTION" [level=3]
      - paragraph: Do not classify critical points by only looking at the graph.
      - list:
        - listitem: Find f'(x) and critical points.
        - listitem: Make a sign chart for f'(x).
        - listitem: Use sign changes or f''(x) to classify.
      - text: Graphs can guide you, but derivatives confirm the result.
